Read 1-fast.md, 2-deep.md, 5-quiz.md (10 shipped items: q001, q002, q004-q009, q011, q012), 3-do.md and 4-say.md (both 'Nothing here yet.'), data/04-organizations/questions.json (12 items: 10 ready, q003 and q010 verified but not shipped), speak.json, tasks.json, cards.json (all candidate), brief.json (traps, signals, slots), the registry entry (bullets 1.1.K1, 1.1.S4, 4.1.K2), FREQUENCY.md (planning input only, never evidence) and the fact records the chapter links. findings.quote: **Twin.** If the stem said "teams create accounts with CreateAccount in a registered OU" instead: enroll those accounts and use Account Factory, because accounts created outside it [are not bound by the registered OU's controls](../facts/control-tower.md#control-tower-accounts-outside-not-bound).
findings.evidence: Fact control-tower-preventive-apply-unenrolled-detective-enrolled-only (docs/controltower/latest/controlreference/preventive-controls): "When you enable controls on an organizational unit (OU) that is registered with AWS Control Tower, preventive controls apply to all member accounts under the OU, enrolled and unenrolled." and (detective-controls): "detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only, not to all member accounts in the OU, if some accounts are not enrolled". The twin tells the reader that an account created with CreateAccount inside a REGISTERED OU gets none of the OU's controls; in fact it already gets the preventive (SCP/RCP) controls and misses only the detective ones. The chapter's own Go deeper block in 2-deep.md ("Preventive controls reach accounts under the OU, enrolled and unenrolled") says the opposite of the twin. A stem of the form 'can an unenrolled account in a registered OU do X that a preventive control denies' would be answered wrong. Fix: "...in a registered OU" instead: the preventive controls already reach those accounts, but detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only, so enroll them (link control-tower-preventive-apply-unenrolled-detective-enrolled-only, display 'detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only').
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): q008 twin now: the preventive controls already reach accounts in a registered OU, but 'detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only', so enroll them (fact added to the question). The explanation now speaks of an OU that is not registered. Explanation and twin only; stem, options and key unchanged, so no new verification is needed.

findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** New accounts created outside Account Factory [are not bound by the registered OU's controls](../facts/control-tower.md#control-tower-accounts-outside-not-bound) until you [separately register the OU or enroll the account](...).
findings.evidence: Five lines later the Go deeper block says, with fact control-tower-preventive-apply-unenrolled-detective-enrolled-only: "Preventive controls reach accounts under the OU, enrolled and unenrolled". The trap callout is the part she reads at a glance (READER.md: 'trusts the gist she gets from one glance'), and its gist is 'unenrolled = ungoverned'. The two AWS pages differ in scope (about-extending-governance speaks of OUs and accounts outside Control Tower; the control reference speaks of a registered OU). Fix: scope the trap to what the exam asks: 'Accounts in an OU that is not registered get no Control Tower controls until you register the OU. In a registered OU, an unenrolled account gets the preventive controls but not the detective ones.' Keep both fact links; the trap entry organizations-trap-control-tower-governs-all-accounts in brief.json needs the same truth wording.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): 2-deep trap rewritten: an OU that is not registered gets no controls until you register the OU or enroll the account (control-tower-accounts-outside-not-bound); in a registered OU, preventive controls reach accounts 'under the OU, enrolled and unenrolled', but 'detective controls apply to enrolled accounts only' (control-tower-preventive-apply-unenrolled-detective-enrolled-only). The duplicate sentence in the Go deeper was removed. The brief trap truth (orchestrator-owned) stays correct for OUs that are not registered.

findings.section: organizations-q005 (Question 5), stem and option c; source data/04-organizations/questions.json
findings.quote: A company has 12 AWS accounts. ... - Create an organization in AWS Organizations from one account, and invite the other accounts to join the organization. ... - Create an organization, create 12 new member accounts in it, ...
findings.evidence: Fact organizations-max-accounts-default-10 (docs/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_reference_limits, table row): "10 — The maximum number of accounts allowed in an organization. This quota is adjustable ... Newly created accounts and organizations might experience a quota below the default of 10 accounts. An invitation sent to an account counts against this quota." The chapter teaches this number in its B-list ("10 | Accounts per organization, adjustable default"). With 12 accounts, the keyed step (create a new organization and invite 11 accounts) cannot complete without a quota increase that no option mentions, and option c creates 12 more accounts. A reader who learned the B-list has a reason to doubt the key; an item writer avoids a stem number that collides with a taught limit. Fix: use 8 accounts in the stem and '8 new member accounts' in option c (the explanation needs no change).
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): A stem change resets the question (R5). An explanation note needs organizations-max-accounts-default-10, which is volatile: q lint refused it (Q112). The key stays the best option, and the account quota is adjustable.

findings.quote: An administrator turned on trusted access for AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) in the AWS Organizations console. When the administrator tries to share the rules with the whole organization, the share fails.
findings.evidence: Lens rule: traps are common beliefs, not trivia. The difficulty-3 item turns on which console created the RAM service-linked role (fact ram-enable-sharing-in-ram-console-not-orgs: "If you enable trusted access with AWS Organizations by using the AWS Organizations console ... the AWSServiceRoleForResourceAccessManager service-linked role isn't created"). That is a setup footnote, not a design decision the SAA-C03 tests; none of the three distractors carries a chapter-04 trap (two carry generic traps, one a misconception). It is also the chapter's only shipped AWS RAM question, while FREQUENCY.md (planning input) reports the RAM sub-topic as 'Sharing TGW or subnets across accounts' (rows 27 and 16). Fix: keep the stem's real decision (share once with the whole organization so future accounts get the rules, versus per-account shares or an account-ID policy) and drop the console detail: e.g. 'sharing with AWS Organizations is enabled in AWS RAM'; or replace the item with a subnet / transit gateway sharing decision (see exam-005).
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): q012 passed the three-lens panel, and its console detail is the documented reason the share fails. A new stem would reset the question. RAM subnet sharing is now covered by shipping q010 (exam-005).

findings.section: organizations-q010 (status verified, not shipped); 04-organizations/1-fast.md signals-and-traps row 6
findings.quote: A network team uses a network account to centrally manage one VPC, including the route tables and the NAT gateways. Application teams in six other accounts of the organization must launch Amazon EC2 instances into subnets of this VPC.
findings.evidence: FREQUENCY.md (third-party research, planning input only) lists RAM under 'Sharing TGW or subnets across accounts' (row 16) and 'Transitive routing, segmentation, PrivateLink, RAM' (row 27). The chapter teaches VPC subnet sharing in the fast signal row 6, the 2-deep RAM table and its Exam trap (organizations-trap-ram-shares-outside-org-any-type), but the only question that tests it, q010 (verified, difficulty 2, core), was not selected; the trap now appears in no shipped question. Fix (orchestrator choice): ship q010 in place of q006 (core, difficulty 1, OrganizationAccountAccessRole on invited accounts, a less frequent topic; difficulty mix becomes 1/7/2, a Q204 warning only), or rewrite q012 as an extended subnet / transit gateway sharing item (exam-004) so both stay core 5 / extended 5.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): q006 set to verified (not shipped) and q010 set to ready (shipped). q lint 04 --ship: no errors, no warnings.

findings.section: changed-recently (first entry); also 04-organizations/2-deep.md numbers-that-decide-answers B-list row 10,240 characters
findings.quote:
> **Changed recently:** (2026-05-15) More SCPs per root, OU or account.
... | [10,240 characters](../facts/organizations.md#organizations-scp-max-document-size) | Size of one SCP |
findings.evidence: Fact organizations-scp-max-document-size, evidence www/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/aws-organizations-increased-scp-quotas: "The maximum number of SCPs that can be attached to a single node (root, OU, or account) has increased from 5 to 10, and the maximum SCP size has increased from 5,120 to 10,240 characters." The same announcement doubled the SCP size, which older practice questions and courses state as 5,120 characters (a classic 'consolidate statements, the SCP is too large' stem). RULINGS hard rule 7 requires a Changed recently note with old value, new value, date and what older questions assume. Fix: extend the first entry to 'More and larger SCPs' with Old 5 SCPs / 5,120 characters and Now 10 / 10,240 characters (both displays exist on the two facts), or add a second entry.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): 1-fast Changed recently entry is now 'More and larger SCPs': Old 5 SCPs of 5120 characters, Now 10 SCPs of 10,240 characters (display request fr-0031 filled).

findings.quote: 4. **Reports by team.** [Only the management account in an organization](../facts/organizations.md#organizations-cost-allocation-tags-management-account) activates cost allocation tags.
findings.evidence: Bullet 4.1.K2 names cost allocation tags and multi-account billing. Tag policies, the Organizations policy type that keeps those tags consistent across accounts, are not taught anywhere in the book (no match for 'tag polic' in data/book.json, _build/registry or any chapter), although two verified facts exist: organizations-tag-policy-standardizes-tags and organizations-tag-policy-enforced-blocks-noncompliant-tagging ("A tag policy can enforce compliance on specified resource types, which prevents noncompliant tagging requests on those resource types from completing", claim). A 'standardize tags across all accounts for cost reports' stem has no home. Fix: one sentence after step 4 (or a Go deeper) with both facts, and one signal row: 'same tag keys in every account' -> tag policy; but not if 'one report per team': activate the cost allocation tag in the management account.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Step 4 of the billing subsection adds 'A tag policy can standardize the tags attached to the AWS resources' (organizations-tag-policy-standardizes-tags). No signal row: the fast signals table has its fixed 6 rows.

findings.quote: q004: **Twin.** If the stem said "keep one account and limit who can change production resources" instead: IAM policies with tag conditions can meet it, because the stem no longer asks for separate accounts. || q001: **Twin.** If the stem said "a role in the management account must not delete a log group" instead: an SCP does not help ...
findings.evidence: Rule: TOOLS-rules.md, strict twins J2 / Q114 are reviewed by the exam-validity lens until implemented; a twin changes one deciding phrase and the key follows. q004: if only that phrase changes, the stem still says 'keep its audit logs in a separate account' and 'apply the same security guardrails to every account that it creates in the future', so 'IAM policies with tag conditions' still fails and the twin's answer is wrong for the stem it describes. q001: the twin replaces the whole requirement (a different principal, a different action, a different account), so it teaches nothing about the deciding phrase of q001. Fix q001: 'If the stem said "no account in the Sandbox OU can leave" instead: attach the SCP to the Sandbox OU, because a Deny reaches all the OUs and member accounts underneath it.' Fix q004: change one phrase that moves the key among the shown options, e.g. 'The company already has an organization and a team that maintains a CloudFormation StackSets baseline' -> the StackSets option, or state the twin with all three requirements removed and label it as such.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): q001 twin now: the Sandbox OU case (a Deny reaches all the OUs and member accounts underneath it). q004 twin now changes one requirement and says the stem then asks for no separate accounts.

findings.quote: | "one bill and shared Reserved Instance discounts" | consolidated billing | ... | one account keeps its discount: turn off its sharing | ... | "run only in approved Regions" | Region deny control, or an SCP with aws:RequestedRegion | ... | per OU: CT.MULTISERVICE.PV.1 [can apply to specific OUs that you specify](...) |
findings.evidence: A 'but not if' guard should name the condition under which the Think answer changes. Rows 3 and 5 name refinements of the same answer (still consolidated billing; still a Region deny control). Row 5 also names 'an SCP with aws:RequestedRegion' without its verified fact organizations-scp-notaction-region-limit-example ("An SCP Deny statement with NotAction and an aws:RequestedRegion condition can limit accounts to approved Regions while exempting the services listed in NotAction", claim), which is the answer when no Control Tower landing zone exists, the more common stem. Suggest: row 5 Think = Control Tower Region deny control; But not if = no Control Tower: an SCP Deny with aws:RequestedRegion (link the fact). Row 3 But not if = a cost report per team: cost allocation tags in the management account.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Row 5 But-not-if is now the case without Control Tower (an SCP on aws:RequestedRegion with the NotAction exception, linked). Row 3 was kept: an account whose sharing is turned off stops receiving the shared discount, so the answer changes.

findings.quote: A company uses AWS Control Tower. The accounts in the Workloads organizational unit (OU) hold Amazon S3 buckets that store audit logs.
findings.evidence: The chapter (2-deep subsection 5, q004 explanation, decision record) teaches that a landing zone keeps logs in the log archive account (fact control-tower-shared-accounts). A Control Tower stem with audit logs in workload accounts reads as a design error and invites the reader to look for 'move the logs to the log archive account'. Also, the Control Tower-native answer ('turn on a preventive control for the Workloads OU') is neither key nor distractor, although the brief slot planned it as the key. Suggest: 'hold Amazon S3 buckets that store application compliance records', and either make the key 'a preventive control (SCP) in AWS Control Tower on the Workloads OU' or keep the SCP key and say why a custom SCP is used.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): A stem change resets the question (R5). The stem is valid as written, and the SCP key is the mechanism of a Control Tower preventive control.

findings.quote: | Question | SCP | RCP | Declarative policy | ... | What does it limit? | [SCPs are principal-centric controls](...) | [RCPs are resource-centric controls](...) |
findings.evidence: The table that holds the chapter's hardest exam distinction (q007/q011 twin pair) ends without the question that decides it. Fact organizations-scp-controls-which-resources-identities-access gives it verbatim: "SCPs provide an ability to control which resources your identities can access." / "RCPs provide an ability to control which identities can access your resources." Suggest a closing line: 'Deciding question: your principals going out (SCP), or anyone coming in to your resources (RCP)?', matching the q007 takeaway.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): The SCP and RCP table ends with the row 'Deciding question' (your people going out: SCP; others coming in: RCP).

findings.section: organizations-q001 (Question 2), Why not for option d
findings.quote: "Replace the AdministratorAccess policy in every member account ...": The administrators can add the action back to their IAM policies, but an SCP limits principals [including the member account's root user](../facts/iam.md#iam-scp-applies-to-member-root-user).
findings.evidence: The 'but' clause does not explain why the option fails; the reader has to infer the link. The decisive fact is already in the question's facts: iam-scp-faq-member-principals-cannot-change-scps ("cannot remove or change SCPs that are applied to that account"). Suggest: 'The administrators can edit IAM policies, so they can add the action back. Principals in a member account cannot remove or change SCPs that are applied to that account.'
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): q001 option d why now: the administrators can add the action back, and principals in a member account cannot remove or change SCPs that are applied to that account.

findings.quote: Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (q001, q004, q005, q007, q008, q009, q011); in the MOST operationally efficient way (q012)
findings.evidence: 8 of 10 shipped questions use the operational-overhead qualifier, including q005, the only task 4.1 (cost) item. The real exam mixes MOST cost-effective, MOST secure and LEAST operational overhead (SPEC.json questions.qualifier_words). Training one qualifier ten times teaches her to stop reading at 'LEAST'. Suggest: when q012 or q006 is rewritten (exam-004, exam-005), give one item a different qualifier, e.g. a RAM item 'MOST cost-effective' (one shared NAT gateway set versus one per account).
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): A different qualifier needs a new or rewritten stem, which resets the question. Note for the drills and mocks.

findings.quote: > **Exam trap:** An Allow for Amazon Athena on the account fails if its OU allows EC2 and nothing else. ... <!-- trap: organizations-trap-account-level-allow-enough -->
findings.evidence: FREQUENCY.md (planning input) names 'SCPs cap permissions but do not grant them' as the first reported sub-topic. The 'grant' half is tested through iam-trap-scp-grants distractors (q005, q012); the 'allow at every level' half (fact organizations-scp-allow-needed-at-every-level) has no shipped question since q003 was not selected, so its trap is in no shipped item. Acceptable for a medium chapter; the Case 2 table and Stop-and-answer partly cover it. Consider q003 for the domain drills or a mock.
findings.resolution: fix-04 (2026-10-13): Note accepted as is. q003 stays verified and is available for drills or a mock.
